correctness.rationale: Properness keeps each color within one independent part. Every vertex outside that part sees every vertex of its color class, forcing the class size odd. Conversely all visible color classes are viewed in full and therefore satisfy every neighborhood parity rule when globally odd. An odd part takes one odd class, and an even part needs two positive odd summands, attainable as 1+(n_i-1). The proof includes size-one parts and r=2, and excludes r=1 where the vertex-neighborhood condition is vacuous. Independent partition enumeration of 23 multipartite profiles totaling <=6 vertices found the exact minima over 2414 canonical colorings.

This exact natural family-wide parity classification is useful as a benchmark; its very short proof and close relation to the definition are openly flagged as a significance limitation, not an unsupported general extension.
